finding.summary: An accepted image turn could remain live-status idle during the final capability read, causing interrupt rejection, later native dispatch, and indefinitely canceling Relay state.
finding.relatedWindow: The same accepted-but-idle assumption existed while reading the pre-turn transcript. Both pre-dispatch windows are covered by the fix.

reproduction: New bridge regression failed against reviewed code: cancel during held transcript preparation returned HTTP 409 instead of 202.

Expanded cross-repository owned-worker smoke failed against reviewed code: holding the final native get_state and canceling left Relay unable to advance the canceled trigger cursor before the bounded timeout.
changes: Bridge distinguishes accepted transcript preparation from adapter dispatch. It can cancel the former locally, releases turn admission and checks the captured turn's interrupted state after asynchronous reads before any dispatch/result overwrite.

Owned worker reserves the pending operation and publishes working before awaiting the final model-capability read. Pre-dispatch interrupt clears/resolves only that operation locally without a native abort.
Late capability responses and request failures verify the original pending-operation identity before dispatching or clearing state, so canceled preparation cannot affect a subsequent turn.
Steering remains unavailable until the native prompt has dispatched; existing uncertain native-interrupt behavior is preserved.

Runtime has a dedicated actual-process regression in its own test suite. The Channels controlled smoke additionally verifies Relay cancellation delivery, cursor settlement, subsequent work while the old read is still held, and no late prompt after release.
